items.title: Strait of Hormuz supply shock
items.detail: Brent +3.0% to $90.79 with transits down to 4 vessels from 8. Roughly a fifth of seaborne crude moves through this chokepoint; a sustained closure is the single largest tail risk in the market right now.

items.title: Semiconductor derating is not finished
items.detail: The semis index has shed more than 20% from its June peak in three weeks. Micron -17%, Intel -21%. The debate has shifted from AI potential to capex monetisation timing, with investment growing roughly 46% faster than sales.

items.title: S&P 500 sitting on its 200-day average
items.detail: Close of 7,475.69 versus a 7,464.61 200-day - a 0.1% cushion. The index has been below its 50-day since 17 Jul. A decisive break would flip the primary trend.

items.title: Energy-driven inflation re-acceleration
items.detail: With crude up roughly 12% on the week, the Fed's July MPR already flags energy as a supply shock keeping inflation above target. Nine of nineteen FOMC dots show a hike by year-end.

items.title: Guidance matters more than beats
items.detail: Netflix beat on EPS and fell about 9% on cautious forward commentary. With two-thirds of reporters beating, the reaction function has moved entirely to outlook - crowded growth names carry asymmetric downside into prints.

items.title: Leadership rotation to defensives and old economy
items.detail: 296 new 52-week highs on Friday led by rail transport, banks and healthcare (UNH, USB, CSX). Broadening breadth is healthy, but the names doing the leading are not the ones carrying index weight.

items.title: Crowded above-target quality names
items.detail: AAPL, VLO, MPC, PANW, CRWD, OKTA and OSCR all trade above or near their average analyst targets. Consensus upside has been exhausted; these depend on estimate revisions rather than multiple expansion.
